exercises.title: Exercise 1 — procedure with OUTPUT parameters: total salary of a department
exercises.problemHtml:
Write proc_SalaryOfDep @depNum INT, @total DECIMAL(12,0) OUTPUT, @numEmp INT OUTPUT: the total salary and the number of employees of the department. RETURN -1 when the department does not exist, 0 otherwise. A department without employees gives total 0 and 0 employees.

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (3 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • Test call: DECLARE @t DECIMAL(12,0), @n INT, @rc INT; EXEC @rc = proc_SalaryOfDep 1, @t OUTPUT, @n OUTPUT;
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Viết proc_SalaryOfDep @depNum INT, @total DECIMAL(12,0) OUTPUT, @numEmp INT OUTPUT: tổng lương và số nhân viên của phòng. RETURN -1 khi phòng không tồn tại, 0 trong trường hợp còn lại. Phòng không có nhân viên cho tổng 0 và 0 người.

Chạy trên SQL SERVER CỦA BẠN, không chạy trong trình duyệt. Máy chấm trong trình duyệt chạy PostgreSQL (WASM) ở chế độ giống SQL Server nên chỉ chấm được SQL chung; bài này cần T-SQL mà chỉ SQL Server thật chạy được (stored procedure, function, trigger, biến, TRY/CATCH, giao dịch…). Trang này không tự chấm: chạy tệp tự kiểm check.sql trên máy bạn, khi nó in ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED thì bấm Tự đánh dấu đã giải.

Cách chạy (Windows hoặc macOS)

Bấm Tải .zip ở khung code rồi giải nén. Thư mục có ba tệp: setup.sql (tạo lại CSDL nháp DBI202_CL với các bảng mẫu), solution.sql (bài làm CỦA BẠN — chỉ sửa tệp này) và check.sql (3 kiểm; in PASS/FAIL từng kiểm và kết thúc bằng ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Luôn chạy đúng thứ tự: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (cài như bài 0.3): mở setup.sql → F5; mở solution.sql → F5; mở check.sql → F5, rồi đọc tab Messages. Hoặc mở terminal trong thư mục (sqlcmd đi kèm SQL Server; chưa có thì winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (đăng nhập SQL thì thay -E bằng -U sa -P "<mật khẩu>").
  • macOS (SQL Server trong Docker như bài 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    rồi cài trình dòng lệnh một lần bằng brew install sqlcmd và, trong thư mục bài:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (hoặc mở ba tệp trong VS Code có extension SQL Server (mssql) và chạy đúng thứ tự đó).

Viết procedure, function, trigger, view bằng CREATE OR ALTER để chạy lại solution.sql bao nhiêu lần cũng được. Khi thi PE thật chỉ nộp lệnh CREATE …, không GO, không lệnh chạy thử.

Yêu cầu

  • Lệnh thử: DECLARE @t DECIMAL(12,0), @n INT, @rc INT; EXEC @rc = proc_SalaryOfDep 1, @t OUTPUT, @n OUTPUT;

exercises.title: Exercise 2 — procedure with a transaction: add an employee to a project, all or nothing
exercises.problemHtml:
Write proc_AddEmployeeToProject @empSSN, @empName, @salary, @depNum, @proNum, @hours, @msg NVARCHAR(300) OUTPUT that inserts the employee AND their assignment to the project. If either insert fails (e.g. the project does not exist), neither row may remain; @msg says "OK: …" or "Error <number>: …".

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (3 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • Both INSERTs inside one transaction in TRY; ROLLBACK in CATCH.
  • @msg starts with "OK" on success and "Error" on failure.

exercises.title: Exercises 3–4 — a scalar function and a table-valued function
exercises.problemHtml:
Write dbo.fn_NumProjects(@empSSN DECIMAL(18,0)) RETURNS INT — the number of projects the employee works on — and dbo.fn_WorkersAtLocation(@locName NVARCHAR(50)) RETURNS TABLE — empSSN, empName, proName, workHours of everybody working on a project located there.

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 4 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (4 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 4 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • Separate the two CREATE FUNCTION with GO.
  • Call with N'TP Hà Nội' — a non-Unicode literal loses the accents and matches nothing.

exercises.title: Exercise 5 — trigger: no employee may earn more than his manager
exercises.problemHtml:
Create tr_Salary_Not_Above_Manager on tblEmployee (AFTER INSERT, UPDATE): an employee (other than the manager himself) may not earn more than the manager of his department; violating statements are rolled back with an error. Trap: Đặng Tuấn Anh already earns 105,000 > his manager's 95,000 — changing only his address must still be allowed (check only salary/department changes).

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 5 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (5 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 5 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • IF NOT (UPDATE(empSalary) OR UPDATE(depNum)) RETURN; then the set-based check.
  • ROLLBACK TRANSACTION + THROW/RAISERROR on violation.

-- solution.sql — YOUR answer for: Exercise 5 — trigger: no employee may earn more than his manager
-- Bài làm CỦA BẠN. Run order / thứ tự chạy: setup.sql → solution.sql → check.sql
USE DBI202_CL;
GO
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER tr_Salary_Not_Above_Manager ON tblEmployee
AFTER INSERT, UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    IF NOT (UPDATE(empSalary) OR UPDATE(depNum)) RETURN;      -- only salary/department changes are checked
    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1
               FROM inserted i
               JOIN tblDepartment d ON d.depNum = i.depNum
               JOIN tblEmployee   m ON m.empSSN = d.mgrSSN      -- the manager's CURRENT row
               WHERE i.empSSN <> d.mgrSSN                        -- the manager himself is not checked
                 AND i.empSalary > m.empSalary)
    BEGIN
        ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
        THROW 50001, N'An employee cannot earn more than the manager of his department.', 1;
    END
END

exercises.problemHtml:
The setup creates tblEmployeeLog(logID IDENTITY, action, empSSN, empName, oldSalary, newSalary, changedAt DEFAULT SYSDATETIME(), changedBy DEFAULT SUSER_SNAME()). Create tr_Employee_Log (AFTER DELETE, UPDATE on tblEmployee) that logs DELETE rows (with the old salary) and SALARY rows (old and new salary) — nothing for updates that do not change the salary.

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (3 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • A deletion = a row of deleted with no partner in inserted.
  • A salary change = inserted JOIN deleted with a different salary.

-- solution.sql — YOUR answer for: Exercise 6 — trigger: keep a log of deletions and salary changes
-- Bài làm CỦA BẠN. Run order / thứ tự chạy: setup.sql → solution.sql → check.sql
USE DBI202_CL;
GO
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER tr_Employee_Log ON tblEmployee
AFTER DELETE, UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    -- rows in deleted without a partner in inserted = real deletions
    INSERT INTO tblEmployeeLog (action, empSSN, empName, oldSalary)
    SELECT N'DELETE', d.empSSN, d.empName, d.empSalary
    FROM deleted d
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted i WHERE i.empSSN = d.empSSN);
    -- salary changes: old and new version side by side
    INSERT INTO tblEmployeeLog (action, empSSN, empName, oldSalary, newSalary)
    SELECT N'SALARY', i.empSSN, i.empName, d.empSalary, i.empSalary
    FROM inserted i JOIN deleted d ON d.empSSN = i.empSSN
    WHERE ISNULL(i.empSalary, -1) <> ISNULL(d.empSalary, -1);
END

exercises.title: Exercise 7 — cursor: raise salaries by working hours
exercises.problemHtml:
Write proc_RaiseByHours that walks with a cursor over the employees of departments 1 and 2 with their total working hours and raises each one: +10% when the total is ≥ 30 hours, otherwise +5%, rounded to whole VND. (Lesson 7.4 shows the one-UPDATE version — here practise the cursor.)

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (3 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • DECLARE … CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR SELECT … LEFT JOIN … GROUP BY …
  • CLOSE and DEALLOCATE at the end.
